title: The land goes to those who fear standing before Allah.
subtitle: The promise after the threat of expulsion
then: The threat was expulsion. The answer: {reward}We will settle you in the land after them.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says this came true when the Prophet ﷺ, once driven from Makkah, later had it opened to him. {idea}It is for whoever fears standing before Allah.{/idea}
now: You are the one pushed out of the team for refusing to fudge the numbers. It feels like losing. {reward}Allah's promise is longer than this week.{/reward} Fear of standing before Him is what keeps your place secure.
old: The ones pushing me out will always have the upper hand.
new: Allah gives the land to those who fear standing before Him.
try: Before one hard choice today, picture standing before Allah, then choose.

title: They asked for victory, and the arrogant lost.
subtitle: When both sides call for the decision
then: After the threats and the promise, {idea}a decision was sought from Allah{/idea}. {trap}Every stubborn, arrogant tyrant who refused His Oneness was brought to loss.{/trap} Ibn Kathir places this within the same story of messengers and their nations.
now: You are in a long argument with your brother, and you are sure you are right, so you will not budge an inch. Ask yourself honestly: {trap}is this conviction, or just stubbornness?{/trap} Pride loses even when it wins.
old: Holding my ground no matter what shows strength.
new: Stubborn pride is what fails in the end; humility before truth wins.
try: In one disagreement today, say: you may be right, let me think about it.

title: Ahead of the arrogant lies Hell.
subtitle: What waits after the loss
then: The verse continues about the arrogant tyrant who refused the messengers. {trap}Hell lies ahead of him, and a foul drink.{/trap} The Quran mentions it soberly, as a warning, so those who hear it can turn back before then.
now: You think of consequences only as far as next month. The verse lifts your eyes further. {idea}What I do now is carried forward.{/idea} That is a warning and also a mercy: there is still time to change course.
old: Whatever happens to me happens in this life only.
new: My choices reach beyond this life, so I take them seriously now.
try: Ask Allah tonight to protect you from the Fire, and name one habit you will drop to that end.

title: Death from every side, yet no dying.
subtitle: A suffering with no exit

row.title: I will deal with it later

then: The description continues for the arrogant who rejected the messengers. {trap}Death comes at him from every side, yet he does not die{/trap}, and still more lies ahead. It is told plainly so that people listening in Makkah, and today, {idea}take the warning while life remains{/idea}.
now: There are nights you wish a problem would just end. This verse describes a place where nothing ends. {reward}Today, every door of repentance is still open.{/reward} Walk through one.
old: There will always be a way out later.
new: The way out is now, in this life, through turning to Allah.
try: Make sincere tawbah today for one specific sin, and ask Allah for His mercy.

title: Deeds without foundation are ashes in a storm.
subtitle: When work is built on nothing
then: Ibn Kathir says this parable is for those who rejected their Lord and built their deeds {trap}on a groundless base{/trap}. They thought they had something, but on the Day {trap}it scattered like ashes in the wind{/trap}, just when they needed it most. He links it to charity spoiled by showing off.
now: You give to charity and post about it. You help a neighbour and mention it later at dinner. {idea}Ask what is under the deed.{/idea} Sincerity for Allah is the ground that keeps it from blowing away.
old: A good deed is good, whatever the reason behind it.
new: Deeds need faith and sincerity underneath, or they blow away.
try: Do one good deed today that no one will ever know about.

title: The One who made the heavens can replace you.
subtitle: Creation in truth, and our dependence
then: Ibn Kathir says this proves the resurrection: the One who made the vast heavens and earth {idea}can easily bring the dead back{/idea}. And if people defy Him, {trap}He can remove them and bring another creation{/trap}. He links it to: you are the ones in need of Allah.
now: You start to feel your mosque, your family, your workplace would fall apart without you. {idea}Allah's work does not depend on any one of us.{/idea} That is humbling, and also freeing: serve because it is an honour, not because He needs you.
old: Things would fall apart without me.
new: Allah needs no one; being used for His work is an honour.
try: Do one act of service today and thank Allah for letting you be the one to do it.

title: None of it is hard for Allah.
subtitle: Replacing a people, raising the dead: easy for Him
then: The short verse closes the thought before it. Ibn Kathir says removing people and bringing others {idea}is not hard or impossible for Allah. It is easy for Him.{/idea} It was said to people in Makkah who doubted they could ever be raised again.
now: You look at your marriage, your debts, your son's anger, and think: this is beyond fixing. For you, maybe. {idea}Not for Him.{/idea} The One who raises the dead can mend what feels dead in your life.
old: Some of my problems are simply impossible.
new: Nothing is difficult for Allah, so I never stop asking.
try: Ask Allah today for the one thing you had stopped asking for because it seemed impossible.

title: Followers and leaders stand together, and no one can help.
subtitle: Blind following, examined on the Day
then: Ibn Kathir describes everyone appearing before Allah {idea}on a flat plain with no cover{/idea}. The followers say to the leaders they obeyed: {trap}can you protect us now?{/trap} The leaders reply: if Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. {trap}There is no escape for us.{/trap}
now: You do something because your favourite influencer does it, or the uncle everyone listens to says it is fine. {idea}No one you follow can stand in for you.{/idea} Pick who you follow as if you will meet them there.
old: If I am following someone respected, it is on them.
new: I answer for my own choices, including whom I follow.
try: Unfollow or mute one voice today that pulls you away from Allah.

title: Shaytan's last speech: do not blame me, blame yourselves.
subtitle: He only invited; you said yes
then: After judgement is done, Shaytan addresses his followers. {reward}Allah's promise was true{/reward}; his was a lie. Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}I had no proof and no power over you. I only called and you answered.{/trap} He disowns them and cannot help.
now: Midnight, alone with your phone, the thought arrives. It does not push your thumb. {idea}It only invites.{/idea} The one who will later say do not blame me is counting on you saying yes now.
new: Shaytan only invites; the choice to answer is mine.
try: Next time a bad whisper comes, say A'udhu billah and do something else for five minutes.

title: Their greeting in the Garden is: Peace.
subtitle: The other side of the same Day
then: Right after Shaytan's bitter speech, the scene turns. Ibn Kathir notes it is the moment judgement is complete. {reward}Those who believed and did good enter gardens with rivers beneath, forever, by their Lord's permission.{/reward} {idea}Their greeting there is peace.{/idea}
now: Your home has days of shouting and slammed doors. Your work has days of blame. {reward}Imagine a place where every word is peace.{/reward} You can practise its greeting now, sincerely, at your own front door.
old: Peace is just a word people say out of habit.
new: Salam is the language of Paradise, and I can speak it here.
try: Say Assalamu alaykum warmly to everyone in your home today, meaning it.

title: A good word is a tree with deep roots and high branches.
subtitle: La ilaha illallah, planted in the heart
then: Ibn Abbas said the good word is {idea}La ilaha illallah{/idea}, and the good tree is the believer. Ibn Kathir cites Bukhari: the Prophet ﷺ asked about a tree like a Muslim, whose leaves do not fall. Young Ibn Umar thought of the answer but was too shy to say it. {reward}It is the date palm.{/reward}
now: You say La ilaha illallah in prayer every day without noticing. Try picturing it as a seed going deeper each time, while your kindness at work and patience at home grow upward like branches. {idea}Root and branch, one tree.{/idea}
old: Saying the shahadah is just a formula.
new: The shahadah is a root that grows into everything I do.
try: Say La ilaha illallah slowly ten times today, thinking about its meaning.

title: It gives fruit in every season.
subtitle: A believer's good never stops
then: The good tree of the last verse {reward}gives fruit at all times, by its Lord's permission{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says this describes the believer, {idea}whose good works rise to heaven by day and by night, summer and winter{/idea}. Allah gives parables so people remember.
now: You are generous in Ramadan and stingy by Shawwal. Kind when rested, short when tired. {reward}A date palm does not take a season off.{/reward} Small steady fruit, even on hard days, is the goal.
old: I do good when I am in the mood or the season is right.
new: A believer gives some fruit in every season, even small.
try: Choose one tiny daily good, like a morning dhikr, and do it today even if you are tired.

title: A bad word is a tree with no roots.
subtitle: Disbelief has nothing to stand on
then: Ibn Kathir says this tree describes {trap}disbelief, which has no base and no stability{/trap}. Anas said it is the colocynth, a bitter plant. {trap}Cut from its root, lying on the ground{/trap}, its works do not rise.
now: Some ideas in your feed sound exciting: a trend, a new life philosophy, a cynical joke about faith. Push on them and there is nothing under them. {idea}Ask of every idea: where is its root?{/idea}
old: A popular idea must have something solid behind it.
new: Ideas cut off from Allah have no root, however tall they look.
try: Next time an idea grabs you online, ask one question: what is this built on?
